Goldman Sachs characterized the Basel III Endgame uncertainty as a factor requiring them to maintain capital cushions above their normal range (specifically running with 90 bps of cushion) to signal flexibility and support client returns while managing regulatory ambiguity. In late 2023, Goldman Sachs also expressed strong opposition to the proposed rules, arguing they went "way too far," would increase credit costs, shift activity to shadow banking, and reduce U.S. competitiveness.

Citi characterized its capital position as "very robust" despite the prevailing uncertainty, noting it ended Q3 2024 with a CET1 ratio of 13.7% (which was $14 billion above regulatory minimums in late 2023). Citi stated that while the ultimate impact would not be known until finalization, they were actively working through mitigating actions and continued to return capital to shareholders, including stock repurchases, on a quarterly basis.
